page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by AWS Graviton3 processors built on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz, accompanied by 256.0 GB of system memory, which establishes an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural component of the r7gd series is the inclusion of 1900 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include discrete hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate notable memory subsystem and parallel execution capabilities. The platform achieves a top-tier score on the PassMark memory suite, supported by strong large-block uncached memory bandwidth of 235.99 GB/sec read and 105.26 GB/sec write. Multi-threaded processing shows solid scalability, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 17567.0 and high throughput in PassMark database operations and static web serving. Conversely, workloads without arm64 optimization or tasks relying on AVX-512 extensions are unavailable on this architecture, and large-scale language model inference exhibits degraded prompt throughput without specialized acceleration.

The dense pairing of 256 GB of memory with 1900 GB of local NVMe storage provides strong resource balance and operational efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads without relying on external block storage volumes. These physical characteristics align directly with memory-intensive and data-heavy environments, including in-memory databases, distributed caches, real-time analytics, and transactional data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by 32 dedicated arm64 AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 cores operating at 2.6 GHz. The server provides 256.0 GB of system memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 15 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, the r7gd.8xlarge shows top-tier memory subsystem throughput with strong multi-core scaling, reaching 235.99 GB/sec read and 105.26 GB/sec write memory bandwidth, alongside robust performance in database operations and static web throughput. Without GPU acceleration, synthetic deep learning workloads exhibit lower generation throughput. The hardware configuration makes the instance well matched for in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput web serving, and low-latency transactional analytics.
